**Privacy‑focused phone settings & app‑permission rules** *(Based on the user’s habit of keeping location services off for most apps – see the location‑privacy guidance from [[summaries/session-05_2025-06-15]])* --- ## 1. Global System Settings (iOS & Android) | Setting | What to do | Why it matters | |---------|------------|----------------| | **Location Services** | **iOS:** Settings → Privacy & Security → Location Services → **Off** (or leave **On** but toggle each app to *Never*).
**Android:** Settings → Location → **Use location** → **Off** (or keep **On** and manage per‑app). | Turns off the OS‑level GPS feed for all apps by default. | | **Significant‑Locations / Frequent‑Places** | **iOS:** Settings → Privacy & Security → Location Services → **System Services** → **Significant Locations** → **Off**. | Stops the system‑level “location arrow” that can appear even when no app is using location [[summaries/session-05_2025-06-15]]. | | **Location‑Based Alerts** (e.g., Weather alerts, AirDrop) | **iOS:** Settings → Privacy & Security → Location Services → **System Services** → **Location‑Based Alerts** → **Off**. | Removes background triggers that would turn on the location indicator without exposing data to third‑party apps. | | **Find My** (device‑tracking) | **iOS:** Settings → [Your Name] → Find My → **Find My iPhone** → **On** (keep for anti‑theft).
**Android:** Settings → Security → Find My Device → **On** (if you need anti‑theft). | Keeps the essential “lost‑device” feature while still blocking other system services. | | **Precise Location (Default)** | **iOS:** Settings → Privacy & Security → Location Services → **Precise Location** → **Off** (global toggle).
**Android:** Settings → Location → **Improve Accuracy** → turn off *Precise location* (or per‑app). | Gives only a coarse location to apps that you *do* allow it, reducing the privacy impact [[summaries/session-05_2025-06-15]]. | | **Background App Refresh / Auto‑Start** | **iOS:** Settings → General → Background App Refresh → **Off** (or limit to Wi‑Fi only).
**Android:** Settings → Apps → *Select app* → Battery → **Background restricted**. | Prevents apps from silently waking up and pulling location while not in use. | | **Widget / Live Activity Permissions** | **iOS:** Settings → Privacy & Security → Location Services → *App* → **While Using the App** (widgets and Live Activities respect this level; they cannot bypass it). | Guarantees that widgets cannot fetch location unless the app has *Always* permission [[summaries/session-05_2025-06-15]]. | --- ## 2. Per‑App Permission Rules ### Core‑function apps (keep location but limit exposure) | App type | iOS setting | Android setting | Recommended level | |----------|-------------|----------------|-------------------| | Navigation / Maps (Google Maps, Apple Maps) | **While Using the App** + **Precise Location** **Off** (use Approximate) | **While app is in use** + **Precise location** **Off** | Allows routing while keeping location coarse. | | Ride‑hailing (Uber, Lyft) | **While Using the App** + **Precise Location** **Off** | Same as above | Needed for pick‑up location but not continuous tracking. | | Weather | **While Using the App** (or *Never* if you accept generic forecasts) | Same | You can also rely on city‑level data without location. | | Emergency services (e.g., 911, SOS) | **While Using the App** (system‑level only) | Same | Required for safety; cannot be disabled. | ### All other apps (default to denial) | Category | iOS | Android | |----------|-----|---------| | Social media, shopping, games, news, finance, health & fitness (unless you use a dedicated tracker you trust) | **Never** (or *Ask Next Time* if you’re unsure) | **Deny** (or *Ask every time*) | | Messaging apps that don’t need location (WhatsApp, Signal, Telegram) | **Never** | **Deny** | | Utility apps (file managers, note‑taking) | **Never** | **Deny** | | System widgets & Live Activities that you don’t use for location | **Never** (or keep *While Using* but ensure you never enable *Always*) | Same | *Key note:* **“Never / Ask Next Time”** is the minimal‑access tier and the default for most apps [[summaries/session-05_2025-06-15]]. --- ## 3. Ongoing Maintenance Checklist 1. **Monthly review** – Open **Settings → Privacy → Location Services** (iOS) or **Settings → Location → App permission** (Android) and verify no app is set to **Allow all the time** / **Always**. 2. **Watch the location arrow** – If the arrow appears unexpectedly, check **System Services** for any newly enabled feature (e.g., “Location‑Based Alerts”). 3. **Update per‑app rules** when you install a new app: set it to **Never** first, then only switch to **While Using** if you discover a functional need. 4. **Backup your settings** – Use iOS’s *iCloud Settings Sync* or Android’s *Google backup* to propagate the same privacy configuration across all devices. --- ## 4. Quick “One‑Tap” iOS Shortcut (optional) Create a Shortcut that: 1. Toggles **Location Services** → Off. 2. Sets **Precise Location** → Off (global). 3. Opens **System Services** → turns **Significant Locations** & **Location‑Based Alerts** → Off. Run it whenever you start a day where you don’t need any location‑based functionality; re‑enable selectively later. --- ### Bottom line - **Start with everything off** (global location, precise location, system services). - **Whitelist only the apps that truly need location**, and even then keep them to **“While Using” + approximate**. - **Regularly audit** the permissions list to catch any accidental “Always” grants. Following these steps keeps the user’s “location‑off‑by‑default” stance consistent across both iOS and Android devices while still allowing the few apps that truly need location to work.

**Short answer:** Bring your phone as usual, but **change the tablet’s location settings first** – otherwise apps or system services on the shared tablet can still broadcast a coarse or precise location (e.g., via the status‑bar arrow or background widgets) and give away where you’re going. **What to adjust on the tablet (iOS or Android)** | Setting | Why it matters | How to set it (based on the guidance from *session‑05_2025‑06‑15*) | |---|---|---| | **App‑specific location permission** | Apps that you don’t need to use on the errand (social, shopping, games, etc.) can leak your whereabouts. | iOS → *Settings → [App] → Location* → **Never** (or *Ask Next Time*).
Android → *App info → Permissions → Location* → **Deny**. | | **“While Using the App” vs. “Always”** | “Always” lets background widgets, Live Activities, or Background App Refresh report location even when the app isn’t open. | Keep apps you need (maps, ride‑hailing, weather) at **While Using**; make sure none have **Allow all the time** (Android) or **Always** (iOS). | | **Precise vs. Approximate location** | Precise location gives exact GPS coordinates; approximate only a city‑level area. | Turn **Precise Location** **off** for all apps that you’ll keep enabled (iOS → *Settings → Privacy → Location Services → [App] → Precise*; Android → *Use precise location* toggle). | | **System services that can trigger the location arrow** | Features like **Significant Locations**, **Location‑based alerts**, and **Find My** can cause the location indicator to appear even when no third‑party app is active. | iOS → *Settings → Privacy → Location Services* → **Significant Locations** → **Off**.
Android → *Settings → Location → Google Location Accuracy* → **Off** (if you want to minimize system‑level fixes). | | **Background App Refresh / widgets** | On iOS, widgets and Live Activities can still request location unless the app’s permission is limited to “While Using”. | Verify that **Background App Refresh** is disabled for apps you don’t need (iOS → *Settings → General → Background App Refresh*). | | **Find My sharing** | If you share your device location with family, they’ll see where the tablet is. | Either temporarily turn off **Share My Location** (iOS → *Settings → [Your name] → Find My → Share My Location*) or make sure the tablet isn’t listed as a shared device. | **Why this works** – The session‑05 summary explains that: - “*Never / Ask Next Time* – minimal access” and “*While Using* blocks background widgets, Live Activities, and Background App Refresh on iOS”【...】. - “*Precise vs. Approximate location* … gives only a coarse location, reducing privacy impact”【...】. - “*System services* … can trigger the location arrow without exposing data to third‑party apps (e.g., Significant Locations, Find‑My)”【...】. By tightening those permissions **before** you start the errand, the tablet will no longer emit location cues that could tip off anyone who looks at it. **Bottom line:** - **Phone:** No change needed if its own privacy settings are already locked down. - **Tablet:** Review and apply the adjustments above; once they’re in place, you can safely bring the tablet along (or leave it at home) without it betraying your early‑morning destination.
